title: Ebola Outbreak in Congo Passes 4,000 Deaths
summary:
Congo is fighting the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak ever recorded. Ebola is a serious disease caused by a virus. Since May 15, more than 8,300 people have gotten sick, and 4,018 have died, health officials said Thursday.

This outbreak is caused by a rare type called Bundibugyo virus. There is no known treatment or vaccine for it yet.

The outbreak is centered in Ituri province, in the northeast. Health workers there are struggling. Some went on strike because they haven't been paid for months. They held signs saying "No money, no data!"

This week, soldiers burned an Ebola camp near the city of Bunia while searching for weapons. About 19,000 people living there had to run away. A UN official said losing the camp means sick people lose the care they need.

More than 50 health workers have died from the virus. One aid worker from Doctors Without Borders got infected and was flown to the Netherlands for special care.

There is a little good news: new cases have slowed down since July. But experts say fighting the disease is still very hard because of violence and because some communities don't trust the health workers.
why_it_matters: It shows how a disease spreads fastest in places with violence, no money for health workers and little trust — problems that decide whether the whole world can stop an outbreak.

keywords.explanation: An outbreak is when a disease suddenly makes many people sick in one place.
A vaccine is a shot or medicine that teaches your body how to fight a disease.
Bundibugyo virus is a rare type of Ebola that has no known treatment or vaccine yet.
A province is a part of a country, a bit like a state in the United States.
A strike is when workers stop working on purpose, usually to demand better pay or conditions.
An aid worker is someone who travels to places hit by disease or disaster to help people.

background_read: Ebola (a dangerous disease caused by a virus that spreads through contact with the body fluids of sick people) is named after a river in Congo, where it was first found.
Congo (the Democratic Republic of the Congo, a very large country in central Africa) has faced several Ebola outbreaks before, and its health workers have a lot of experience fighting the disease.

Doctors Without Borders (a group of doctors and nurses who travel to places hit by outbreaks, wars and disasters to treat patients) treated an infected worker who was flown to the Netherlands for special care.
The United Nations (a group where almost all countries work together on big world problems) has officials who warn when people lose the care they need.
Article_Structure: WHO: Ebola patients in Congo, health workers in Ituri province, soldiers searching for weapons, and aid workers from Doctors Without Borders — more than 50 health workers have died from the virus.
WHAT: The fastest-growing Ebola outbreak ever recorded has passed 4,000 deaths, with more than 8,300 cases and 4,018 deaths since May 15.
WHERE: Ituri province in northeastern Congo, especially around the city of Bunia, where a camp for about 19,000 people was burned.

WHY: There is no known vaccine or treatment for this rare Bundibugyo virus, health workers are unpaid and striking, violence is destroying care camps, and some communities do not trust the health workers.

perspectives.description: They are risking their lives with little protection, and some went on strike holding signs saying 'No money, no data!' because they have not been paid for months.
They say that when a camp is burned and about 19,000 people run away, sick people lose the care they need, which makes the outbreak even harder to stop.
New cases have slowed down since July, but experts say violence and a lack of trust in some communities still make fighting the disease very hard.
